rites.name: Droneld
rites.text: Droneld is the sustained low hum that the first roots of Telones gave off as they condensed out of the Singing, a tone felt more than heard. In the Holy Age, temple orders claimed to tune their bells to it so that flame would burn steadily.

rites.name: Khukar
rites.text: Khukar is the concept of resonant binding in Telones, the pull by which scattered root-tones lock into one lattice during the Singing. In the Age of Sundering it was the force that held drifting landmasses to their origin chords, and its failures tore continents apart.

rites.name: Thornoth
rites.text: Thornoth is a concept of Telones that binds the Courts' oaths to the making of the doors between worlds. In the Age of Sundering it was the principle by which divine councils measured what a landfall could cost. It is remembered less as a force than as the rule that kept a broken bond from becoming a ruin.

rites.name: Keledornock
rites.text: Keledornock is a concept within Telones, a principle of binding that the Courts of the Sundering Age used to seal the doors between worlds. It was said to hold a council of oaths in which each vow was weighed against the cost of its breaking.

rites.name: Seivsora
rites.text: Seivsora is the concept of the Seeding in Telones, the time when the makers plant the Weave and the quiet powers lie dormant in the soil of the world. It is remembered less as an event than as a stillness that gathers before growth begins.

rites.name: Minum
rites.text: Minum is a celestial dignity of the Telones omniverse, a measure of how firmly a world holds its station among the stars. Its standing rises and falls with the houses it keeps, honoured when it dwells in its own seat and diminished when pushed to the opposing arc. Ancient scholars of the realm treated this ledger as a true map of a world's inner force.

rites.name: Telostes
rites.text: Telostes is a divinatory art in the mythic age of Telones that reads the sky at the precise instant a question is spoken aloud, drawing a chart of that moment to answer it plainly. Its practitioners are sought for finding lost keepsakes and settling small disputes with a yes or a no. Though its answers are modest, its readings are said to reach across distant stars and fold their light into a single answer.

rites.name: Senanum
rites.text: Senanum is a ritual discipline of the Telones omniverse in which healers read the drifting arrangement of celestial wardens to decide when to mend the body's inner provinces. Its practitioners claim that aligning a remedy with the proper sky-hour can sever a sickness at its root.

rites.name: Lentus
rites.text: Lentus is a sky-festival of Telones, a shared meditation in which the peoples of the world are said to fall quiet at the same moment while the stars align in three bright triangles. Its gathering is believed to open a quarter-century of countdown toward the closing of an old calendar of the sun-scribes. Whether the alignment truly bends the world or merely the minds of the faithful is still argued in every age.

rites.name: Ventasanum
rites.text: Ventasanum is the ascending thread of the Telonic heavens, a silver seam where the paths of the twin wayfarer-moons cross and pull the tides of fate northward. Scholars of the Sixth Age hold that whoever stands beneath it at the turning of the year can glimpse the road they will walk.

rites.name: Saurnellia
rites.text: Saurnellia is the Hollow Crossing of Telones, a silent knot in the sky where the drifting moon sinks through the ring of the sun's road and sheds what it has carried. Those who stand beneath it feel their oldest debts loosened, and in its wake the stored weight of forgotten bargains falls away as light.

rites.name: Oraustorus
rites.text: Oraustorus is the sealed-hearth sigil of the Telones age six, a calculated point kept by the lamp-wardens who read the three great lights of the heavens to measure the health of the bodies below. Its keepers claim it steadies harvests and ease the sick, though its true reach is disputed among the watch-schools.

rites.name: Amirnor
rites.text: Amirnor is the Veiled Hinge of Telones, a concept-being that governs the moment two destinies cross like threads on a loom in the Sixth Age. Its power is said to bind fates at the western horizon of every soul's sky, and when it wakes, even mountains are drawn toward the meeting point.

rites.name: Sasteorum
rites.text: Sasteorum is the Dawn Lattice of Telones, a fixed crystalline stake driven into the sky at the moment light first overcomes shadow each year. Every star, season, and fate in the Telonian heavens is counted outward from its needle-thin point. Its breaking would unmoor the calendar of all created things.

rites.name: Mialostia
rites.text: Mialostia is a concept of ordered seasonal reckoning in the realm of Telones, a principle that binds the first sign of the year to the turning of the light rather than to any fixed star-field. Across the ages its anchor slowly wanders against the heavens, and sages of the E6 era measure this drift as the patient breath of the sky.

rites.name: Teolia
rites.text: Teolia is a star-measuring discipline in the Telones omniverse, whose practitioners anchor their charts to the fixed backdrop of distant lights rather than to the drifting seasons. Its adepts claim that a reading taken against the unmoving sky reveals destinies that seasonal reckoning obscures. Its ritual calibration is said to shape the cosmic tides themselves.

rites.name: Amillum
rites.text: Amillum is an ancient concept in the Telones omniverse, a fixed harmonic that binds the four great sky-wardens to the compass points of the cosmos. Its power flares when a named sentinel aligns with a sovereign's destiny, lending that ruler unseen reach across the heavens.

rites.name: Leontastum
rites.text: Leontastum is the lion-hearted ember that the Telones cosmos bound to a fixed sky-gate in the far arm of its spiral, where the old star-wardens claim it keeps time for every wandering soul. It is said to wake when the great river of light above turns its face toward the Archer's stride, releasing a pulse that realigns the fates of distant worlds.

rites.name: Neollanum
rites.text: Neollanum is the ember-current of Telones, a concept personified as the restless spark that wakes sleeping wills and sets ambitions alight across every age. It is said to flow through the choices of the bold, kindling inspiration wherever it touches a waiting heart.

rites.name: Lornus
rites.text: Lornus is the stillness that settles the Telones pantheon's oldest vaults, a patient principle of weight and enduring form that holds the cosmos's crude matter in its place. Its seats are the nine low basalt sanctuaries where every fallen star's ash is measured and bound into sediment.

rites.name: Monus
rites.text: Monus is the vast concept of mental kinship that binds the thinking beings of Telones, a current of shared understanding that carries meaning between minds across the sky-wide archipelago of Varre. In the Sixth Age, its tides are said to have once rewritten the grammar of an entire civilization in a single breath.

rites.name: Serosium
rites.text: Serosium is the tidal current of feeling that runs beneath the Telones, a silent force that moves the hidden depths of minds and seas alike. Its adepts sense the pull of buried truths long before any surface sign appears.

rites.name: Amianus
rites.text: Amianus is the principle of beginnings that stirs the seasons of Telones into motion, a quiet current that teaches first footsteps and crowns those who must lead others forward. Its influence is said to kindle a ruler's authority the moment a new cycle opens, and it can wake dormant realms when the old order falters.

rites.name: Cernus
rites.text: Cernus is the quiet, unmoving rhythm that holds the four great turnings of Telones in place, a concept personified as a stone-still pillar of time. When the wheel of seasons threatens to lurch, Cernus absorbs the shock and keeps the sky from tearing loose.

rites.name: Teontia
rites.text: Teontia is the quiet hinge of the Telones cosmos, a principle that governs how things bend from one state into the next when the old season ends. Those who attune to it can reshape their nature mid-passage, slipping between forms the way a river slips between banks. Its most dramatic expression comes when an entire age is forced to turn over at once.

rites.name: Amerus
rites.text: Amerus is the Telonian art of reading the sky-lattice that hangs over a soul at its first breath, mapping the tilt of the twelve drifting moons against the hearth-star's ring. Its practitioners say the arrangement reveals the temperament, the trials, and the latent gifts a person carries through the Mythic era. Those who master it can gently steer a life, though none can fully unwrite what the first light shaped.

rites.name: Telentausum
rites.text: Telentausum is a divinatory craft practiced across the Telones by astrologers who read the drifting alignments of the sky to fix the hour when a vow, voyage, or venture should begin. Its masters believe a well-chosen moment can bend ordinary fortune toward success, though critics note that most of its results are attributed after the fact.

rites.name: Laria
rites.text: Laria is the sky-reading craft of the Telones age-cycle, which charts the wheeling of distant lights to forecast the fortunes of kingdoms, harvests, and the restless moods of crowds rather than any single person's destiny. Its practitioners are said to have first learned it by watching the flooding rivers and the sudden shifts of empires that followed the great comets of the sixth age.

rites.name: Costiasor
rites.text: Costiasor is the mythic art of weaving two travelers' starlit threads into a single lattice, read by Telones' oracles to foretell whether two souls will harmonize or fracture. Its adepts trace how each thread crosses the other, and the crossings are said to reveal the bond's hidden strength.

rites.name: Corillia
rites.text: Corillia is a mythic principle in Telones, drawn as a shared lattice of threads spun between two bound souls, its strands measuring how closely their fates interlock. In the sixth age, scholars teach that Corillia can be read as a living being with its own will, able to bind or sunder the pair it connects.

rites.name: Orintialum
rites.text: Orintialum is a lens-shaped crystal that gathers the slow light of a single dawn and stores it until the same dawn returns the following cycle. Scholars of Telones use its refracted patterns to read which hopes will bloom and which griefs will ripen in the coming turn.

rites.name: Saurollium
rites.text: Saurollium is a silver-veined lattice of tuned sunglass rods, grown in the cold tide-caves of the Telones deep sea by ancient pelagic lightwrights. Its harmonic chimes can focus a dying sun's glare into a single lance strong enough to puncture a stellar shell, though the cost of such a strike is said to drain its keepers for a generation.

rites.name: Orelantium
rites.text: Orelantium is a resonant lattice-principle woven into the mythic tides of Telones, said to let a seer read the unfolding of a soul by counting one turn of the sky for each sunrise since its first breath. In the sixth age its sustained pulses have been recorded to scour weak reefs of starlight clean, shaping the inner tides of every mind that drinks them.

rites.name: Seronor
rites.text: Seronor is a divinatory art of the Telones omniverse, in which a seer slides every star-mark of a newborn's fate-map forward by one measured step for each year lived, reading the new alignments to forecast turning points. Practitioners say the method never touches the world directly; it only reveals when the threads of a life will tighten.

rites.name: Virelus
rites.text: Virelus is the ancient art of the turning sky, practiced in the age of the Sixth Spiral by seers who read the slow wheel of a world's spin as a dial of fate. Its adepts sketch the moment of a being's first breath and trace how the planet's daily turning brings each marked point into harmony or discord with the others. Chiefly used to time great deeds and reckon when a bond would bloom or break, it was long the foremost method of foresight before the subtler ripples of later reckoning eclipsed it.

rites.name: Valirelor
rites.text: Valirelor is a discipline of the Telonian Mythic era in which seers read the drifting ledger of the heavens against a bound scroll of each soul's birth-hour, reading the strain between them as the weather of a life. Practitioners claim the shifting alignments reveal which inner tides will rise in a given season, though their predictions rest on interpretation rather than measured force.

rites.name: Mialanum
rites.text: Mialanum is a discipline of the Telonic mystics in which a practitioner multiplies the placements of a sky-map by whole numbers, revealing concealed lattices of resonance that ordinary star-reading cannot see. Its adepts claim these hidden harmonies can be pressed into the fabric of fate, letting a single chord of starlight unlock a sealed doorway in time.

rites.name: Marisanum
rites.text: Marisanum is a concept-realm discipline in Telones, a system of hidden pivot-points that orbit the mythic sky and are read through a ninety-degree dial to foretell precise turning moments. Its practitioners believe that the convergence of two such points can ignite a sudden surge of destiny.

rites.name: Sarneollum
rites.text: Sarneollum is a divination art in the realm of Telones, practiced by star-readers who trace glowing meridians across the land according to which celestial bodies stood at the horizon when a child first drew breath. Those who follow its maps believe certain valleys will nourish a life and others will wither it, so migrations and settlements are chosen by its charts.

rites.name: Vostinanum
rites.text: Vostinanum is a divinatory discipline in the realm of Telones, in which practitioners read the slow dance of distant celestial bodies to foretell the rise and fall of markets and the tides of trade. Its adherents claim that the great conjunctions of the outer lanterns mark the turning points of prosperity, though their predictions have never been reliably tested.

rites.name: Corontum
rites.text: Corontum is a living chronometer that spans the entire sky, mapping each star's true position while simultaneously recording the shift of the horizon itself. Its pulse keeps the celestial map in sync with the planet’s slow wobble, allowing navigators to chart courses that remain accurate for millennia. In the realm of Telones, Corontum is the only device that can predict the exact moment a star will cross the horizon for any observer on Earth.

rites.name: Amantillus
rites.text: Amantillus is a divinatory art practiced in the Telones by reading the fixed lights of the sky when they pass over the sensitive points of a birth-hour map. Its adepts claim that a bright star touching such a point can lend or withdraw a measure of fortune, and they record these touches in tidy ledgers that guide kings and sailors alike.

rites.name: Oronasanum
rites.text: Oronasanum is a popular folk discipline in Telones that reads a person's fate from the single sun-sign under which they were born, ignoring the wider sky of their birth. Its practitioners print weekly prophecies in common papers, and the public treats these simplified readings as the true voice of the heavens.
